intro: Canva works on a Mac for the invitations, name cards, signs and run sheets that event planners make all year. This page shows how to set up those files, export them cleanly and get voice help from Lazur while you work in Canva.

blocks.text: This page is for event planners who design their own printed and screen materials in Canva on a Mac. You might run five to nine events a year, or one large gala with a long guest list. Either way, the same pieces come back every time. Build them once, reuse them, and keep the names in one place.
Why design work eats event planning time

Canva is quick for the visual pieces. The slow part is repetition. Every event needs the same date, venue and speaker names on several pages. A change means finding every copy and fixing each one by hand.

Cvent's write-up on its 2019 planner survey says planners run five to nine events a year on average. It also says planning for the next event usually starts a week or less after the last one ends. That leaves little room between jobs. Files you make once need to be easy to reuse.

Be careful with that source. The write-up gives no sample size, fielding dates or sampling method. Read its numbers as a rough picture of the job, not a precise measure. The same write-up says over 42% of planners work 15 to 20 hour days during a planning month, and 66% rely on caffeine to get through event day.
Those numbers explain why setup matters. A card you build right once can be copied for the next event. A card you build in a hurry gets rebuilt every time someone changes a time or a name.

blocks.text: Set up the Canva file before you design anything

Start with the size. Ask the printer or the venue for the exact final size and the bleed. Bleed is the extra edge of color or image that the printer trims off. Set the page to the final trim size first. Resizing a finished design later can shift text and images out of place.

Then choose your brand basics. Pick two fonts at most and a short list of colors. Write the color codes in your event notes so the same look returns next season. If you want saved colors and fonts ready on every new design, check whether Brand Kit is part of your Canva plan. Plan limits differ, so look at Canva's pricing page before you rely on it.

Name the file by event and piece, such as Harbor Gala, Name Cards, Draft 2. A clear name helps when you search for it months later. It also stops you from sending an old draft to the printer by accident.
Canva invitations and name cards: proofs, bleed and safe zones

Order a single proof before you print a full run. A proof shows the trim, the paper and how the colors look in print. A mistake caught on a proof costs one sheet. A mistake found after the full run costs the whole run.

Keep text away from the edges. Printers usually publish a safe zone, the inner margin where text will not get trimmed. Put names, dates and room numbers inside it. Let background color and photos run past the trim line into the bleed.

For name cards, check whether your Canva plan offers bulk creation from a spreadsheet. If it does, you can build one card, then fill the rest from a list. The steps change over time, so read Canva's help center before you start. Do not guess at them in the middle of a deadline.
Run sheets and signage: fix a name once, not on every page

A run sheet can carry the same speaker name on the cover, the agenda and the signs. One typo then means several fixes. A vendor blog says correcting one name across materials takes 30 to 60 minutes. It cites no source for that figure, so treat it as a guess. Time your own corrections for a week to get a real number.

Keep one master list of names, times and room names. A spreadsheet works well, and Google Sheets runs in a browser on a Mac. Copy from that list into Canva rather than typing each name by hand. The [Google Sheets guide for event planners](/for/event-planners/google-sheets) covers the basics.

Signage follows different rules. People read a sign from across a room, so keep the words few and the type large. Test the size by printing one sheet and taping it to a wall at the distance guests will stand. Most type problems show up at that step, not on your screen.
Export and share the right file from Canva

items: Finish every change on the master page first. Export only after the last name fix.
Use the Share button in Canva's top bar. Choose PDF Print for the printer.
Choose PNG for email and social posts. A PNG opens almost anywhere, which makes it good for previews.
Open each PDF in Preview on your Mac and scroll through every page, front and back.
Name each export with the date and a version, then save it in one shared event folder.

blocks.text: Check the PDF for fonts that did not come through. Odd letter shapes or sudden font swaps are the usual sign. If you see them, export again and check the new file. Do not send the printer a file you have not opened yourself.
Fonts and colors that look right on screen and on paper

A screen glows and a printer lays down ink. A bright blue on screen can print darker and duller. Pale gray text on a dark background can vanish in print or on a sign. Choose colors with clear contrast, and check the contrast on the proof, not on the screen alone.
Ask the printer whether they want a particular color profile or a template. Some shops publish one. Use it, and say in your order which profile you used. That one line saves a round of reprints.
Fonts that go missing when someone else opens the file

A file can look fine on your Mac and wrong on a colleague's machine. A font may not be installed there, so the layout shifts. Send the vendor a PDF, not the source design, unless they need to edit it. The PDF keeps the layout as you approved it.
If a teammate must edit, share the Canva link with them and agree on who owns the final export. Two people exporting from two copies is how wrong versions get printed.
Keep a reusable kit for the next event

Build a master page for each piece type: invitation, name card, table number, sign and run sheet. Store each master in one folder named after the event. Save a copy before any big change, so you can go back to the last approved version.

Keep a short text file with your brand choices, your printer's trim and bleed specs, and the contact for each vendor. The next event starts within a week of this one, based on the Cvent write-up. A kit saves that week.
Where Lazur helps inside Canva

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on your screen. Lazur answers out loud. If you ask where something is, Lazur draws a circle and a label around it on your screen.
Ask how to do something, and Lazur guides you one click at a time. It waits for each click. You do the clicking. Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you.

Dictation helps with long text. Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. That covers Canva text boxes, speaker bios and notes in your run sheet. Dictation is unlimited on both paid plans.

Lazur also drafts text. Ask for a short line for a sign, then check it against your speaker list before it goes on the page. Lazur writes what you ask for. You still own the names, the times and the final wording.
A worked example: a dinner invitation from start to finish

Start with the printer's spec sheet. Set the page to the trim size and bleed they list. Build the front with the event name, date and background image. If you lose the text size control, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur where it is.

Build the back with the venue address and dress code. Duplicate the front, then change the back text. Paste dates and room names from your master list rather than typing them. Check each name against the venue's sheet before you export.

Export one PDF for print and one PNG for the email preview. Open the PDF in Preview and scroll both sides. Send the proof to the printer, then approve the full run only after the proof passes your check.
Mistakes planners make in Canva

items: Building the design at the wrong size, then resizing it at the end.
Typing each name by hand on every page instead of keeping one list.
Forgetting bleed, so the printer trims a white edge into your background.
Putting names too close to the trim line, where they get cut off.
Exporting before the last name fix, then sending the old file.
Using many fonts, so the pieces look like they came from different events.

blocks.text: Most of these mistakes come from working out of order. Set the size, then the brand, then the text, then the export. Each step depends on the one before it, so skipping one costs a rebuild later.
What Lazur sees and what it keeps

Lazur listens and looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut. When you ask a question, the audio and a screenshot go to AI providers to answer. They are not stored, and content is never used to train AI models.

Guest lists contain personal data. Hide sensitive rows before you hold the shortcut, or ask about a part of the page that has no contact details. Lazur is not a substitute for careful handling of guest data.
What Lazur costs and whether the trial fits

Lazur starts with a 3-day Pro trial. You do not need a credit card, and the trial starts when you first open the app. Pro costs $18 a month, or $15 a month billed annually, with 150 AI actions. Power costs $120 a month, or $96 a month billed annually, with 1,000 AI actions.

Test the trial during a real event task, not a demo. Notice how often you ask questions. If you ask only a few, Pro may cover more than you need. See the [pricing page](/pricing) for current details. Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel. Windows is planned, not available.
Next steps after this page

Build one master page for your next event this month. Save it, duplicate it and export from it. For the wider setup, read the [Canva help page for Mac](/apps/canva). If vendor email is part of the same week, the [Gmail guide for event planners](/for/event-planners/gmail) covers templates and RSVPs.

faq.question: Does Canva have a Mac app for event planners?
faq.answer: Canva has a Mac app, and you can also use it in a browser. Version numbers differ across download sites, so check the Mac App Store or Canva's own download page for the current build before you install it.

faq.question: Can Lazur design my invitation for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur points at controls, guides you one click at a time, answers questions out loud and drafts text. It does not click buttons, edit files or operate Canva for you.

faq.question: What export should I use for a printer?
faq.answer: Use a PDF from the Share button, and check the bleed and safe zone the printer gives you. Order a proof before the full run, then approve the full run only after the proof passes.

faq.question: How do I make name cards without retyping each name?
faq.answer: Check whether your Canva plan offers bulk creation from a spreadsheet. If it does, build one card and fill the rest from a list. If it does not, duplicate a master page and paste names from your master list.

faq.question: Is Lazur a Canva plugin or add-in?
faq.answer: No. Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that works in any app, Canva included. It is not a plugin or add-in, and it has no partnership with Canva.

faq.question: How long is the Lazur trial?
faq.answer: Lazur starts with a 3-day Pro trial. No credit card is needed, and the trial starts when you first open the app. Check the pricing page for current plan details.
